gen-gf-warnes-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro reads plainly, a plain sans with gaps at its terminals. Warnes stretches out above it in tapered ink strokes with no stroke contrast at all, and that loud spacing is the pair's whole personality.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-roboto: Roboto brings generous mouths on its round letters and a lowercase that sits close to cap height. And Warnes, with rounded strokes like cut lengths of cord, is the one built to be looked at, while the body simply carries the words.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-ruda: Ruda has a sizable x-height and a wire-like monoline skeleton, so its lowercase feels open and approachable. Ruda then lets Warnes, stretched and tapering and bold, do all the shouting while it quietly holds the lines together.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-saira: Saira keeps a visible gap in each s and rounded letters that stretch high toward the top line, which makes it steady company. Long stretches read smoothly.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-sarpanch: Flat fineliner lines, spaced out and bold: that's Warnes, set against Sarpanch with its clearly open lowercase e. Paragraphs in it would flow easily.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-tiktok-sans: Snowburst One looks like a stencil sheet, with wide bridges between its tall letters. TikTok Sans, in sans-serif form, has an x-height near cap height, so a modest size for it is enough.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-vend-sans: Pipe-cleaner strokes, wide terminal openings, outsized lowercase: that is Tektur, loud and a bit odd. And Vend Sans, drawn with a ruler-straight constant line, can be set fairly small since its x-height fills the line.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-yaldevi: Yaldevi reads like a plain sans with an e whose eye opens clearly to the right and generously sized lowercase. Unica One sits above in single-nib strokes. Paragraphs move along easily.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-sintony: Sintony reads like a plain sans with a chunky, tall midzone and curves that never clog up. Tilt Neon adds tube-like, bold bowls above it, and the two share the same sturdy build.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-sofia-sans: Commanding lettering comes from Wallpoet, with a line where the paper shows through between letters. And Sofia Sans, a sans-serif of constant-width strokes and tall, open rounds, keeps the text beneath it level-headed.
